verses.rationale: Keeps the immense crowd, physical pressure, priority to the disciples, and yeast-hypocrisy identification.
verses.before: Meanwhile, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so many that they were trampling one another. Jesus began speaking first to his disciples: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
verses.after: Meanwhile, a crowd of many thousands gathered, so that they were trampling one another. Jesus began by speaking first to his disciples: “Guard yourselves against the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Meanwhile, when so many thousands of the crowd had gathered that they were trampling one another, he began to say first to his disciples, “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired concealed/revealed and hidden/known claims.
verses.before: Nothing is covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not become known.
verses.after: Nothing is concealed that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not become known.
verses.tsw_comparator: But nothing is covered up that will not be revealed, nor hidden that will not be known.

verses.rationale: Makes the private-to-public movement audible while retaining darkness, light, and rooftops.
verses.before: Therefore whatever you have said in darkness will be heard in the light, and what you whispered in someone’s ear in private rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops.
verses.after: So whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you have whispered in private rooms will be proclaimed from the rooftops.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore whatever you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what you have whispered in the ear in inner rooms will be proclaimed upon the housetops.

verses.rationale: Retains Jesus’ address as friends and the killers’ limited power.
verses.before: “I tell you, my friends, do not fear those who kill the body and after that can do nothing more.
verses.after: I tell you, my friends, do not fear those who kill the body and after that can do nothing more.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And I say to you, my friends, do not fear those who kill the body and after that have nothing more that they can do.

verses.rationale: Preserves death, authority, Gehenna, repetition, and the unresolved identity in the wording.
verses.before: I will show you whom to fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to throw into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
verses.after: But I will show you whom to fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to throw into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will show you whom you should fear: fear the one who after he has killed has authority to cast into Gehenna; yes, I tell you, fear him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact numbers, low price, and divine remembrance.
verses.before: Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins? Yet not one of them is forgotten before God.
verses.after: Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins? Yet not one of them is forgotten before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Are not five sparrows sold for two coins? And not one of them is forgotten before God.

verses.rationale: Retains the concrete image, reassurance, and comparison.
verses.before: Even the hairs of your head have all been counted. Do not be afraid. You are worth more than many sparrows.
verses.after: Why, even the hairs of your head are all counted. Do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
verses.tsw_comparator: But even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Do not fear; you are of more value than many sparrows.

verses.rationale: Preserves reciprocal public acknowledgment and the heavenly audience.
verses.before: I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before people, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before God’s angels.
verses.after: I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before God’s angels.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And I say to you, everyone who acknowledges me before people, the Son of Man will also acknowledge him before the angels of God,

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrasting reciprocal denial.
verses.before: But whoever denies me before people will be denied before God’s angels.
verses.after: But whoever denies me before others will be denied before God’s angels.
verses.tsw_comparator: but the one who denies me before people will be denied before the angels of God.

verses.rationale: Retains the asymmetry and explicit forgiveness language.
verses.before: Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
verses.after: Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
verses.tsw_comparator: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but the one who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

verses.rationale: Names all three forums and the two concerns without softening the legal setting.
verses.before: When they bring you before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not be anxious about how or what you should answer or what you should say,
verses.after: When they bring you before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say,
verses.tsw_comparator: And when they bring you before synagogues and rulers and authorities, do not be anxious about how or what you should answer or what you should say;

verses.rationale: Keeps the Spirit’s timely instruction and necessity.
verses.before: because the Holy Spirit will teach you in that hour what you should say.”
verses.after: for the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you must say.”
verses.tsw_comparator: for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that hour what you ought to say.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the familial dispute and direct demand.
verses.before: Someone in the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
verses.after: Someone in the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And someone from the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the blunt address and both judicial roles.
verses.before: Jesus said to him, “Man, who appointed me a judge or divider over you?”
verses.after: But Jesus replied, “Man, who appointed me judge or arbitrator over you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said to him, “Man, who appointed me a judge or divider over you?”

verses.rationale: Retains double warning, all greed, life, abundance, and possessions.
verses.before: Then he said to them, “Watch out and guard yourselves from every kind of greed, because a person’s life does not consist in the abundance of possessions.”
verses.after: Then he said to them, “Watch out and guard yourselves against every kind of greed, because a person’s life does not come from having an abundance of possessions.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Take care and guard yourselves from all covetousness, because one’s life is not in the abundance of his possessions.”

verses.rationale: Keeps wealth, land, and fruitfulness as the setup.
verses.before: He told them a parable: “The land of a certain rich man produced abundantly.
verses.after: He told them a parable: “A rich man’s land produced an abundant crop.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he told a parable to them, saying, “The land of a certain rich man produced abundantly.

verses.rationale: Preserves interior deliberation and storage problem.
verses.before: He began reasoning within himself, ‘What should I do? I have nowhere to store my crops.’
verses.after: He thought to himself, ‘What should I do? I have nowhere to store my crops.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And he was reasoning within himself, saying, ‘What shall I do, because I have nowhere to gather my crops?’

verses.rationale: Keeps demolition, enlargement, and comprehensive hoarding.
verses.before: Then he said, ‘I will do this: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and goods.
verses.after: Then he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and goods.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, ‘I will do this: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will gather all my grain and my goods.

verses.rationale: Retains self-address, long security, and four imperatives.
verses.before: I will say to my life, “You have many goods stored up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.”’
verses.after: Then I will say to myself, “You have many goods stored up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.”’
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will say to my soul, Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years; rest, eat, drink, be merry.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the divine address, immediate death, demanding-back image, and ownership question.
verses.before: But God said to him, ‘Fool! This very night your life is being demanded back from you. The things you prepared—whose will they be?’
verses.after: But God said to him, ‘Fool! This very night your life is being demanded back from you. Then who will have what you prepared?’
verses.tsw_comparator: But God said to him, ‘Fool! This night your soul is required of you; and the things you have prepared—whose will they be?’

verses.rationale: Keeps self-directed accumulation contrasted with wealth toward God.
verses.before: So it is with the one who stores up treasure for themselves and is not rich toward God.”
verses.after: So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So is the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the inference and parallel life/body needs.
verses.before: Jesus said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you: do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
verses.after: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life—what you will eat—or about your body—what you will wear.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to his disciples, “Therefore I say to you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will wear.

verses.rationale: Keeps both comparative claims.
verses.before: Life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
verses.after: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.

verses.rationale: Retains ravens, agricultural and storage details, divine feeding, and comparison.
verses.before: Consider the ravens. They neither sow nor reap, they have neither storeroom nor barn, yet God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds!
verses.after: Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap; they have no storeroom or barn, yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than birds!
verses.tsw_comparator: Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have neither storehouse nor barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than the birds!

verses.rationale: Preserves the source’s measurement image and its possible life-span sense.
verses.before: Which of you by being anxious can add a single cubit to your span of life?
verses.after: Which of you by worrying can add a cubit to your span of life?
verses.tsw_comparator: And which of you by being anxious is able to add a cubit to his span of life?

verses.rationale: Keeps the argument from inability and calls the task small.
verses.before: If you cannot do even this small thing, why be anxious about the rest?
verses.after: If, then, you cannot do even this very small thing, why worry about the rest?
verses.tsw_comparator: If then you are not able to do even a small thing, why are you anxious about the rest?

verses.rationale: Preserves flowers, work images, Solomon, glory, and clothing comparison.
verses.before: Consider the lilies, how they grow. They neither labor nor spin, yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
verses.after: Consider how the lilies grow: they neither labor nor spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
verses.tsw_comparator: Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither labor nor spin; yet I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.

verses.rationale: Keeps grass’s brevity, oven, divine provision, and rebuke.
verses.before: If God clothes the grass this way—alive in the field today and tomorrow thrown into an oven—how much more will he clothe you, you of little trust!
verses.after: If God clothes the grass this way—alive in the field today and thrown into an oven tomorrow—how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith!
verses.tsw_comparator: But if God so clothes the grass, which today is in the field and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith!

verses.rationale: Retains the ongoing pursuit and unsettled anxiety.
verses.before: Do not keep seeking what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be unsettled.
verses.after: So do not keep seeking what you will eat and drink, and do not be anxious.
verses.tsw_comparator: And do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be unsettled.

verses.rationale: Preserves nations’ pursuit, Father language, and known need.
verses.before: The nations of the world seek all these things, but your Father knows that you need them.
verses.after: For all the nations of the world pursue these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all these things the nations of the world seek, but your Father knows that you need them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the priority and promised addition.
verses.before: Instead, seek his kingdom, and these things will be given to you as well.
verses.after: Instead, seek his kingdom, and these things will be given to you as well.
verses.tsw_comparator: Instead, seek his kingdom, and these things will be added to you.

verses.rationale: Retains tenderness, flock image, Father’s pleasure, and gift.
verses.before: Do not be afraid, little flock, because your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
verses.after: Do not be afraid, little flock, because your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Do not fear, little flock, because your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.

verses.rationale: Keeps the concrete economic commands and thief-moth heavenly contrast.
verses.before: Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Make yourselves moneybags that do not wear out, an unfailing treasure in heaven, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
verses.after: Sell your possessions and give to those in need. Make purses for yourselves that do not wear out—an unfailing treasure in heaven, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sell your possessions and give alms; make for yourselves purses that do not grow old, an unfailing treasure in the heavens, where no thief approaches nor moth destroys.

verses.rationale: Preserves treasure-heart relation.
verses.before: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
verses.after: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
verses.tsw_comparator: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

verses.rationale: Renders girded waists naturally while retaining readiness and lamps.
verses.before: “Keep your belts fastened and your lamps burning.
verses.after: Be dressed and ready, with your lamps burning,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning,

verses.rationale: Keeps servants, delayed wedding return, knock, and immediate welcome.
verses.before: Be like people waiting for their master to return from a wedding banquet so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him immediately.
verses.after: like servants waiting for their master to return from a wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they can open the door for him at once.
verses.tsw_comparator: and be like people waiting for their master when he returns from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him immediately.

verses.rationale: Preserves reversal in which the master serves the watchful servants.
verses.before: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds watching when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will fasten his own belt, have them recline at the table, and come serve them.
verses.after: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds awake when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve, have them recline at the table, and come serve them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are those slaves whom the master will find watching when he comes; truly I say to you that he will gird himself and have them recline at table and will come and serve them.

verses.rationale: Keeps both night watches and continued readiness.
verses.before: If he comes in the second watch or even the third and finds them ready, blessed are they.
verses.after: Even if he comes in the second or third watch of the night and finds them ready, those servants are blessed.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if he comes in the second watch, or even in the third, and finds them so, blessed are those.

verses.rationale: Retains unexpected thief, precise hour, and breached house.
verses.before: But understand this: if the owner of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
verses.after: But understand this: if the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
verses.tsw_comparator: But know this, that if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have allowed his house to be broken into.

verses.rationale: Keeps readiness, unexpected time, and present-future force.
verses.before: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.”
verses.after: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You also, be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.”

verses.rationale: Preserves named speaker and audience question.
verses.before: Peter said, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us or to everyone?”
verses.after: Peter asked, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everyone?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Peter said, “Lord, are you telling this parable for us or also for all?”

verses.rationale: Keeps stewardship, household responsibility, and timely food distribution.
verses.before: The Lord said, “Who then is the faithful and wise steward whom the master will put over the household to give them their food allowance at the proper time?
verses.after: The Lord replied, “Who then is the faithful and wise manager whom the master will put in charge of his household servants to give them their food allowance at the proper time?
verses.tsw_comparator: And the Lord said, “Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom the master will set over his household to give the portion of food at the proper time?

verses.rationale: Retains blessing on active faithfulness.
verses.before: Blessed is that servant whom the master finds doing so when he comes.
verses.after: Blessed is that servant whom his master finds doing so when he comes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed is that slave whom his master will find doing so when he comes.

verses.rationale: Keeps solemn assurance and enlarged trust.
verses.before: Truly I tell you, he will put that servant over all his possessions.
verses.after: Truly I tell you, he will put that servant in charge of all his possessions.
verses.tsw_comparator: Truly I say to you that he will set him over all his possessions.

verses.rationale: Names abuse of both men and women and the servant’s indulgence without softening harm.
verses.before: But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My master is taking a long time to come,’ and begins beating male and female servants and eating, drinking, and getting drunk,
verses.after: But suppose that servant says in his heart, ‘My master is taking a long time to come,’ and begins to beat the male and female servants, and to eat, drink, and get drunk.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if that slave says in his heart, ‘My master delays in coming,’ and begins to beat the male and female servants, and to eat and drink and become drunk,

verses.rationale: Retains surprise, violent judgment image, and association with the unfaithful.
verses.before: the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know. He will cut him in two and assign him a place with the unfaithful.
verses.after: That servant’s master will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know. He will cut him in two and assign him a place with the unfaithful.
verses.tsw_comparator: the master of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in pieces and appoint his place with the unfaithful.

verses.rationale: Keeps knowledge, failure to prepare and obey, and severe punishment.
verses.before: That servant who knew the master’s will but did not prepare or act according to it will receive many blows.
verses.after: That servant who knew his master’s will but did not prepare or act according to it will receive many blows.
verses.tsw_comparator: And that slave who knew his master’s will and did not prepare or do according to his will will receive many blows,

verses.rationale: Preserves degrees of responsibility, corporal image, gift, trust, and demand.
verses.before: But the one who did not know and did things deserving blows will receive few. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required, and from the one entrusted with much, even more will be demanded.
verses.after: But the one who did not know and did things deserving blows will receive few. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required; and from the one entrusted with much, even more will be demanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: but the one who did not know and did things worthy of blows will receive few. Everyone to whom much has been given, much will be required, and from the one to whom they entrusted much, they will demand more.

verses.rationale: Retains the disruptive fire image and difficult expression of desire.
verses.before: “I came to cast fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
verses.after: “I came to cast fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
verses.tsw_comparator: “I came to cast fire upon the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!

verses.rationale: Keeps baptism as impending ordeal, constraint, and completion.
verses.before: But I have a baptism to undergo, and how distressed I am until it is completed!
verses.after: But I have a baptism to undergo, and how distressed I am until it is completed!
verses.tsw_comparator: But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!

verses.rationale: Preserves the startling denial and division.
verses.before: Do you think I came to give peace on earth? No, I tell you, but rather division.
verses.after: Do you think I came to bring peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you think that I have come to give peace on earth? No, I tell you, but rather division.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact household number and balanced opposition.
verses.before: From now on five in one house will be divided, three against two and two against three.
verses.after: From now on, five people in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.
verses.tsw_comparator: For from now on five in one house will be divided, three against two and two against three;

verses.rationale: Retains every reciprocal family division and specific relationships.
verses.before: They will be divided: father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”
verses.after: They will be divided: father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”
verses.tsw_comparator: they will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”

verses.rationale: Keeps western cloud, immediate forecast, and fulfillment.
verses.before: Jesus also said to the crowds, “When you see a cloud rising in the west, you immediately say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and it happens.
verses.after: He also said to the crowds, “When you see a cloud rising in the west, you immediately say, ‘A rainstorm is coming,’ and so it happens.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he was also saying to the crowds, “When you see a cloud rising in the west, immediately you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.

verses.rationale: Preserves wind direction and heat.
verses.before: When the south wind blows, you say, ‘There will be scorching heat,’ and it happens.
verses.after: And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It will be scorching hot,’ and it happens.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when you see the south wind blowing, you say, ‘There will be scorching heat,’ and it happens.

verses.rationale: Retains accusation and weather-time contrast.
verses.before: Hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of earth and sky. Why do you not know how to interpret this present time?
verses.after: Hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of earth and sky, but why do you not know how to interpret this present time?
verses.tsw_comparator: Hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you do not know how to interpret this time?

verses.rationale: Keeps direct appeal to moral judgment.
verses.before: And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?
verses.after: Why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?
verses.tsw_comparator: “And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

verses.rationale: Preserves legal sequence, urgency, and escalating custody.
verses.before: As you go with your accuser to a magistrate, make every effort to settle with them along the way, so that they do not drag you to the judge, the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
verses.after: As you go with your accuser before a ruler, make every effort along the way to settle with him. Otherwise he may drag you before the judge, the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as you go with your accuser to the magistrate, make an effort to settle with him on the way, lest he drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic negation and exacting final payment.
verses.before: I tell you, you will certainly not get out until you have paid the last small coin.”
verses.after: I tell you, you will certainly not get out until you have paid the very last small coin.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I tell you, you will certainly not come out from there until you have paid the last coin.”

verses.rationale: Preserves timing, Pilate’s violence, blood, and sacrificial setting.
verses.before: At that time some people were present who told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
verses.after: At that very time, some people arrived and told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now there were some present at that time who were telling him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

verses.rationale: Keeps the comparison and rejects suffering as proof of greater sin.
verses.before: Jesus answered them, “Do you think these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans because they suffered these things?
verses.after: He answered them, “Do you think these Galileans were worse sinners than all other Galileans because they suffered this way?
verses.tsw_comparator: And answering, he said to them, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the Galileans because they suffered these things?

verses.rationale: Preserves denial, repentance, universality, and warning.
verses.before: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
verses.after: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
verses.tsw_comparator: No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact number, location, accidental death, and guilt comparison.
verses.before: Or those eighteen people on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think they were worse offenders than everyone else living in Jerusalem?
verses.after: Or those eighteen people on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think they were more guilty than everyone else living in Jerusalem?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they were worse offenders than all the people living in Jerusalem?

verses.rationale: Retains repeated denial and warning.
